text:
pagerbot: ALERT fired: prod-usw2 inference-gateway 5xx-error-rate > 300% (5m window) — auto-page to oncall. symptom: high 502/504 ratio, spike started ~1766666600. pager id: PD-87933 :rotating_light:

Carol (oncall): acked. I'm looking. any customer-facing incidents? :eyes:

Maria (support): I've got a few incoming chats reporting failures from EU customers (CNTRL-142). Likely impacting some update flows but not every customer.

Dave (sre): quick check: Grafana shows a sharp increase in 502s on the inference gateway fronting Dedicated pools, concentrated on hostgroup: ded-pool-usw2-b. Could be a rate-limiter or upstream stall.

Jess (infra): I see weird TCP retransmits on the LB -> pool path around the same timeframe. Not classic CPU or OOM on GPUs.

Alex (eng): any deploys around then? I don't see a code push in the last hour from CI.

Carol (oncall): runbook step 1: confirm error signature. I've pulled a few sample traces; most 502 responses have "upstream reset" and short-lived KV cache misses in the LRU logs.

Dave (sre): interesting — KV cache eviction storms can domino into synchronous DB reads and then timeouts. Could also be a load-pattern change (burst of long sequences). Querying metrics: 
```
sum(rate(http_errors_total{job="inference-gateway",code=~"5.."}[1m])) by (region)
```
Shows prod-usw2 at +430%.

Jess (infra): I'll increase LB connection pool size and temporarily relax keepalive settings on the proxy tier to see if retransmits drop. Pushing a one-line config bump now.

pagerbot: PD page escalated to engineering after 120s (unacked) — adding Dave (sre) and Jess (infra) to the page.

Maria (support): Heads-up: two customers on Dedicated have active requests failing. I'll open a high-priority support note and flag Sales for possible outreach.

Alex (eng): can we warm a fallback route to dedicated-readonly or to the smaller quantized model? If the full model runtime is getting stuck waiting on external I/O, a faster variant could preserve availability.

Carol (oncall): good idea. Dave, can you trigger a routing rule to send 20% of traffic to model-quantized-v1 as a canary? We want to see if errors fall for that slice.

Dave (sre): initiating routing change: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: routing-overrides
data:
  prod-usw2-weight: "0.8,0.2" # primary, fallback
EOF
```
Applying...

Dave (sre): routing change applied. Observability: tailing the metric — 5xx rate for the primary pool is still elevated but overall 5xx across region drops ~12% (initial).

Jess (infra): LB config bumped; keepalive increased from 60s to 300s, connection retries lowered. Respawned proxy sidecars on affected nodes to pick up config.

Carol (oncall): runbook step 3: collect logs for one failing request and paste trace id. anyone have a trace id?

Alex (eng): grabbed trace id from a failing call: trace=tx-9a7b3c. Payload shows: long stall waiting for retrieval from embeddings-store, then net/http: timeout awaiting response -> upstream reset. Looks like the embeddings-store (external cache) returned 503 a few times.

Dave (sre): embeddings-store evictions exploded at the same time — TTL churn + load spike. There was a sad pattern: many requests with unique prefixes (low cache hit), causing high QPS to embeddings-store.

Maria (support): customers reporting degraded UX (timeouts) but not data loss. I'll update the status page with a note: "Partial degradation in inference responses for some customers in US-WEST-2; mitigation in progress."

pagerbot: Auto-remediation suggestion: scale ded-pool-usw2-b by +3 replicas (policy: emergency-scale). Would you like me to run? :robot_face:

Carol (oncall): please do the scale. Also add a temporary rate-limit on non-critical routes (batch ingestion) to reduce pressure.

pagerbot: Scaling ded-pool-usw2-b +3 initiated — pods launching. Also applying route-based rate-limit: 
```
POST /alpha/control/rate-limits
{"route":"/v1/embeddings:ingest","limit":"100r/s"}
```

Jess (infra): after scale and rate-limit, 5xx rate is trending down — now +80% vs baseline. We should be able to fully mitigate if the cache hit pattern improves or we add a short-lived fetch-backoff.

Alex (eng): I'll add a backoff on cache-miss paths in the client lib to avoid thundering herd. Patch queued to PR, will hotfix if needed.

Carol (oncall): customer impact assessment: partial; impact window so far ~15 minutes, affecting a subset of Dedicated customers with ingestion-heavy workloads. No PII exposure. Severity: SEV-2 for now. ETA to full resolution: 30-45m contingent on cache stabilization.

Dave (sre): note: one pod failed liveness during scale due to a transient OOM in sidecar; I restarted it. Keeping an eye on memory.

Maria (support): Sales and customer success notified. Posting brief to #customer-impact with recommended copy.

pagerbot: PD note: escalation suppressed after ack and active mitigation. Keep monitoring.

Carol (oncall): transitions: I'm on initial triage. If anyone needs to hand off, say now. Otherwise we'll keep this thread as main coordination.

Jess (infra): I'll continue infra follow-ups and monitor LB telemetry for 10 more minutes, then hand to Dave for postmortem.

Alex (eng): prepping a short repro harness to simulate the unique prefix pattern and see if our client-side backoff removes the spike. Will post PR link.

Dave (sre): tentative action items: (1) postmortem draft (assign to me), (2) consider small TTL increase and jitter in cache, (3) add histogram alarms for embeddings-store latency, (4) add fallback route in routing layer as permanent runbook.

Carol (oncall): ack. I'll update PD with a note and then remove myself from rotation once stable. Current status: mitigation in progress, error-rate falling, partial customer impact.

Maria (support): updating status page and customers. I'll re-open if we see re-regression.

pagerbot: Closing auto-page state to "monitoring" after human ack + mitigation. Will re-open if 5xx returns above threshold.

Carol (oncall): final note: assigning follow-ups: Dave (postmortem), Alex (client hotfix), Jess (infra config change), Maria (customer comms). If we stay stable 40m, we'll mark incident resolved and notify customers. :white_check_mark:
